accuracy.evidence: Qualities and the repair idea were checked against the DfE Relationships Education statutory guidance (2019) 'Caring friendships' bullets (characteristics of friendships such as truthfulness, trustworthiness, loyalty, kindness and sharing; most friendships have ups and downs that can be worked through), the PSHE Association KS1 Relationships theme and the IB PYP PSPE interactions strand cited by the topic. No claim says a fall-out always ends well or that children must accept every apology; safety advice is left to the trusted-adult lessons.

misconceptions.evidence: Aimed at documented 5 to 7 year old beliefs: friendship as a transaction ('Only if you give me your car', challenge 'only plays if you give her sweets'), a fall-out ends a friendship forever (challenge tag over, mastery m2), a good friend gets their own way (bossy tags and the Play fair prediction), fibbing after an accident (hide and lie tags), and choosing a new offer over a promise (Honest and true prediction, break tag).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfriend is built around friendship qualities and repair: pinning quality badges on one friend, choosing between fair and bossy play, owning up and keeping a promise, sequencing calm down, sorry, play again, and spotting the unfriendly frame. flagcare matches kind acts to strangers' needs, flagentry rehearses joining a game, flagshare is turn-taking with objects; none sequences a repair or rejects quality badges. The shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Bossy and Says mean things badges bounce off the friend with a reason, so the child finds the four good qualities by trying. The fix step refuses Say sorry before Take a big breath with 'First calm down', so the order of repair is discovered, then confirmed by the done text. The strip step makes the child look at faces and words to find bossy, exclusion and whispering.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'always gets their own way' when games clash (many children equate the best friend with the one who decides), and 'Go with Ben. Sam will not mind' for a broken promise. Each task right after makes the child pick turn-taking and keeping the promise, and the done line quotes their guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers (bossy, deal, over, lie, hide, out, mean, break). because() returns a specific correction for each, for example 'Friends have ups and downs. You can make up and be friends again.' for 'Yes, forever', and every wrong tap in the lab names the slip via WHY or ORDER_WHY.

readability.evidence: Kid text is FK 0.0 against the family kid limit of 5.0, with sentences like 'Take a big breath. Say sorry.' Adult text is FK 6.9 against 10.0 and uses the exact terms from the guidance: caring friendships, trustworthiness, loyalty, reliability, inclusion, ups and downs, repair, plus Key Stage 1 and the IB PYP interactions strand.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with the kindness, joining-in, sharing and roles lessons is under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph is one quality group (kind and joining, fair, honest and promises, making up); adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, the qualities model, four named mistakes with a caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360x640 light and iPhone 13 dark: the friend figure sits above six large wrapped badges in two rows, scene steps show a speech box and three tall choice cards, the strip shows three tall frames with two faces and a caption each, and the young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall. phone_sweep reported 0 findings on iPhone and Android in both themes.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every Show me completed on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark, and there were no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button twin (one button per badge, per choice, per repair step, Picture 1-3 with spoken captions), and the canvas aria-label is updated with each message.
